programme: No single recognisable module ties the twelve factors together. The strongest individual node, NCOR1, does carry a real, nameable complex on its own — its target list includes its own paralog NCOR2/SMRT, the corepressor scaffold proteins TBL1X and TBL1XR1, the opposing coactivator CREBBP, and the nuclear receptors AR, ESR1 and RARB — i.e. the canonical NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 corepressor circuit that sets steroid/retinoid receptor output. GRHL3 separately carries an epithelial-barrier/differentiation programme (CDH1, TFAP2A, SMAD7, CLDN7). But these two are mechanistically unrelated complexes, and the remaining ten factors (developmental Nodal/TGF-beta signalling via FOXH1, calcineurin-NFAT cardiac stress signalling via NFATC4, AP-1 fibrotic signalling via FOSL2, CREB-family stress response via ATF1, ETS-family GABPA, chromatin regulators ZMYND8/ASH1L, homeobox factors TLX1/LBX1, and coactivator TCF20) do not converge on either of these or on each other. Twelve factors that co-occur across patient groups are not, here, a module.
role_in_a: No consistent role can be assigned across the set. If anything is separately plausible from general biology it is NCOR1's corepressor complex acting on cardiac nuclear-receptor/metabolic gene programmes, but nothing in the retrieved record places NCOR1, or any of the other ten factors, in cardiovascular disease.
role_in_b: NCOR1 and GRHL3 individually have hedged literature placing them in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (epigenetic marker candidacy for NCOR1; epithelial/Wnt-AKT axis regulation for GRHL3), but they act through different mechanisms and neither is corroborated by the rest of the list.
shared_axis: None proposed. A TGF-beta/fibrosis story built from FOXH1 (Smad partner), NFATC4 and FOSL2 (Smad-cooperating stress/fibrotic TFs) would be the obvious reach here, but its natural hub, SMAD4, was removed as tissue-generic — its absence is diagnostic of why that narrative doesn't hold, not an oversight to patch over.
reasoning: Open Targets returns no cardiovascular association for any of the eleven factors, so there is no anchor on the disease-A side at all. On the disease-B side only NCOR1 and GRHL3 have papers that plausibly concern esophageal cancer, and even those are explicitly hedged by the reader as not establishing a functional or causal role; every other retrieved paper is off-topic (colorectal, hepatocellular, pancreatic, cervical, lung cancer) or non-mechanistic (a structural 22q13 duplication case series for TCF20). The factors themselves span unrelated pathways (nuclear-receptor corepression, Nodal/TGF-beta development, calcineurin-NFAT, AP-1, CREB, ETS, two chromatin enzymes, three homeobox/developmental TFs), and the one plausible unifying reach — a Smad/TGF-beta fibrotic axis — is undercut by SMAD4's removal as tissue-generic. Twelve factors recurring across patient groups is a real statistical pattern, but it is not evidence of a shared mechanism here.
support: PMID 41208974 (candidate epigenetic marker signature in ESCC listing NCOR1, functional role unclear); PMID 42243308 (GJB6-GRHL3 feedback loop attenuating ESCC progression via AKT signalling); PMID 36442813 (GRHL3/HOPX/Wnt/beta-catenin axis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma); PMID 28912415 (ATF1 targeting inhibits proliferation/migration, title implicates esophageal cancer but abstract truncated and uncertain); PMID 38956246 (GABPA autoantibody used in an ESCC diagnostic ML model, not a mechanistic study); PMID 40583527 (TCF20 22q13.2 duplication case series listing cardiovascular abnormalities among many systemic findings, structural genetics not mechanism). None of these connect cardiovascular disease and esophageal cancer to each other through a shared factor or pathway.
how_to_falsify: Take NCOR1 and GRHL3, the two factors with any textual grounding, and test whether their ChIP-seq/knockdown regulons overlap beyond chance in a cardiac tissue dataset and an ESCC line; if the two programmes show no shared target enrichment (as their distinct biology predicts), that confirms there is no unifying module here rather than an artefact of incomplete literature retrieval.
caveats: Blood vs esophagus is an anatomically and developmentally distant pairing with no obvious shared cell type. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 184 patient-group comparisons, so counts like NCOR1's 98/184 reflect repeated subgroup slicing of the same two cohort pairs, not 98 independent replications — treat the recurrence fractions as weaker evidence than the raw numbers suggest. The single-view exclusions (GATA6, ARID1B, ZNF217, etc.) show what a subgroup-driven story would have looked like, and this account avoids relying on them. The tissue-generic exclusion of SMAD4 in particular removes the node that would otherwise make a TGF-beta/fibrosis narrative tempting; its absence should be read as the filter working, not as missing support to reinstate.
